newsitem.title: CANADA: Manitoba hog marketer extends price plan to Friday.
newsitem.headline: Manitoba hog marketer extends price plan to Friday.

text.p: A month-long extension of a one-price-for-all hog pricing formula was extended to Friday while Manitoba's largest marketer pursues pricing contract talks with three of the province's four packers, the Winnipeg Free Press said.

Manitoba Pork, which markets 80 percent of the provincial hog output, concluded a long-term pricing contract with Manitoba's largest packer, Maple Leaf Foods Inc packer Burns Meats Ltd last Friday, the report said.
The old contract ended January 31 but was extended through February and then extended to March 7 for the other packers.
Early last month, hog processing ground to a near standstill as the packers refused to purchase under a scheme similar to the Chicago Mercantile Exchange's lean hog index.

The point of contention was a C$10/cwt freight deduction that would price hogs FOB Winnipeg rather than Chicago. Packers were reluctant to absorb the freight differential, Manitoba Agriculture Minister said at the time.
Manitoba's packers slaughter 6,500 to 7,000 hogs a day.
"On Friday we'll again have to reassess where we are with each one on an individual basis," Manitoba Pork assistant general manager Rene Chabidon said in the Winnipeg Free Press.
"Hopefully we'll have one or two more (contracts) signed," Chabidon said.
Talks continue with packers Schneider Corp, Jack Forgan Meat Ltd and Springhill Farms.
